lessons.summary: If the input becomes "many", what prints?
explanation: On a Result, ? extracts the Ok value or returns early with the Err, converting its error type if needed. The enclosing function must have a compatible return type; ? is not a panic or an instruction to ignore errors.

text.parse::<u32>() requests an unsigned32-bit integer. The ::<...> syntax supplies a type argument explicitly. ParseIntError is the parser’s error type. use std::num::ParseIntError brings that standard-library name into this scope; it does not download a dependency. lessons.title: String boundaries and Unicode
lessons.summary: If the range changes to 0..1, what prints on the second line?
explanation: String and str are UTF-8 text. len reports bytes, while chars iterates Unicode scalar values. A scalar value is not always a whole user-perceived character; grapheme segmentation needs additional rules.

str.get(range) returns Option<&str> and rejects out-of-range indices or non-character-boundary byte positions. Direct indexing with an invalid range can panic. In "éa", é occupies two bytes, so 0..2 selects it but 0..1 splits its encoding.

Expected output or behavior: 3 2
Some("é"). Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: HashMap ownership and entry APIs
lessons.summary: If the second word becomes "write", what is the read count?
explanation: HashMap<String, u32> owns its String keys. insert moves an owned key into the map; borrowing a key for lookup is a different operation. Hash-map iteration order is not a stable presentation order.

entry(key).or_insert(0) obtains mutable access to the existing value or inserts zero first. *count dereferences that mutable reference so += 1 updates the stored number. Repeating the same key updates one entry rather than making duplicates. get returns Option<&u32>; copied turns a present borrowed integer into its Copy value, and unwrap_or(0) supplies zero only when the Option is None.
Expected output or behavior: 2. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

lessons.title: HashSet and uniqueness
lessons.summary: If the second insertion is "Go", what prints?
explanation: HashSet stores distinct values according to equality and hashing. insert reports true for a newly added value and false when an equal value was already present. It does not preserve insertion order for iteration.

len counts unique stored values; contains tests membership without removing anything. This example prints scalar facts instead of asserting a random hash iteration order. String slices here refer to static literal text.

lessons.title: Modules visibility and paths
lessons.summary: If pub is removed from label, what happens?
explanation: mod creates a module. Public visibility is opt-in with pub; a private function inside a child module is not accessible from its parent. A path such as helper::label names an item through its module.
use brings a name into scope; it does not fetch a dependency. crate:: starts at the current crate root. This inline-module example needs only one main.rs file and the standard library.

lessons.title: Cargo packages and dependency boundaries
lessons.summary: If the local library returns n * 3, what prints after rebuilding?
explanation: A Cargo package has a manifest and one or more targets such as a binary or library crate. Edition selects language rules; it is not the compiler version. This fixture explicitly chooses edition2024 and only a local library dependency.

Save the files below, put the complete main example in src/main.rs, then run cargo run --offline --quiet from the package directory. path points to supplied local source rather than a registry. Offline does not conjure missing dependencies: all required sources must already be present.
```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "lesson_app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
[dependencies]
lesson_math = { path = "localmath" }
```
```toml
# localmath/Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "lesson_math"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
```
```rust
// localmath/src/lib.rs
pub fn double(n: u32) -> u32 { n * 2 }
```

Complete local Rust example; the app itself does not execute it:
```rust
fn main() { println!("{}", lesson_math::double(6)); }
```
